configurations.name: without_skill
configurations.description: Baseline without skill (general Claude capabilities only)

analyst_observations: The skill improves pass rate from 40% to 94% (+54 percentage points), demonstrating strong value for structured Jenkins build diagnosis.

The only failing assertion in with_skill (eval-2 log timestamp) is a compliance gap — the agent saved the log as 'linux-ci-466.log' without the required timestamp suffix. This suggests the SKILL.md instruction for timestamped naming could be made more prominent.
Baseline pass rates cluster around 30-50% — the baseline correctly diagnoses root causes but lacks structured workflow (config paths, KB search, Epic fast-path, timestamped logs).

With_skill runs are ~43% slower on average (278s vs 194s), largely due to the additional phases (path resolution, KB search, source code context). Eval-2 with_skill was especially slow (380s) because it was the only run that successfully executed curl.exe downloads.

Tool denial affected 2 of 3 with_skill runs (evals 1 and 3). Despite this, the skill's structured output format and KB integration were still demonstrated from cached data. In production (where tools are allowed), all assertions would likely pass.

Non-discriminating assertions: 'Produced diagnosis with root cause' passes for both with_skill and baseline in all evals — both correctly identify the error. The discriminating assertions are config-path resolution, KB search, Epic fast-path, and timestamped log naming.
The baseline outputs are in Chinese (matching user language) while with_skill outputs are in English. This is a style difference, not a correctness issue, but worth noting for user preference.
